title: PSK31, QPSK and Varicode
idea: PSK31 sends data by jumping the phase of one steady tone. QPSK uses four phases, two bits per jump. Characters go out in Varicode, where common lowercase letters are short and capitals are long.

rows: 0, 90, 180 and 270 degree shifts, one per pair of bits
Sideband sensitive, error correcting, about the same bandwidth as BPSK31
Longer Varicode sequences, slower to send

compare.how: Two phases (0 and 180), one bit per symbol.
Four phases, two bits per symbol, same 31.25 baud.
Short codes for common letters; capitals take longer.

traps.wrong: Upper case letters are sent with more power
traps.why: Capitals aren't louder; they just have longer codes, so they take longer.
Viterbi is a way of decoding error correction, not the character code.

traps.wrong: Modulation using quasi-parallel to serial conversion to reduce bandwidth
traps.why: Made-up words. QPSK is four phase shifts for pairs of bits.
